title: Find Customers with No Phone Number
description:
Some customers did not provide a phone number when they signed up. Find everyone whose phone is missing.

**Table: customers** — `id`, `name`, `email`, `phone`

Return `id`, `name`, and `email` for all customers where `phone` IS NULL. Order by `id`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INT, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR, phone VARCHAR); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Alice Smith','alice@example.com','555-1234'),(2,'Bob Jones','bob@example.com',NULL),(3,'Carol White','carol@example.com','555-5678'),(4,'Dave Black','dave@example.com',NULL),(5,'Eve Green','eve@example.com','555-9012'),(6,'Frank Brown','frank@example.com','555-3456'),(7,'Grace Lee','grace@example.com',NULL),(8,'Hank Miller','hank@example.com','555-7890');
solution_sql: SELECT id, name, email FROM customers WHERE phone IS NULL ORDER BY id

test_cases.description: 3 customers (Bob, Dave, Grace) have no phone number

hints: NULL cannot be compared with = or !=. Use IS NULL to check for missing values.
WHERE phone = NULL will never match any row — always use IS NULL.
explanation: NULL represents the absence of a value. The only correct way to test for NULL is with IS NULL (or IS NOT NULL). Equality operators like = NULL always return unknown/false in SQL. Customers 2 (Bob), 4 (Dave), and 7 (Grace) have NULL in the phone column.
